documents.t: The account-deletion page is up, and its flow has not yet passed a live deletion test. It is a signed-in self-service path that asks you to use the Google account linked to Waylock, confirm that sign-in again and explicitly confirm deletion. Deletion then waits 7 days. Sign-in stops during that wait, and you can cancel on the same page or on Account. Removal comes on or soon after the date shown, in your time zone. The website and in-app paths need verification; an uncertain response does not prove that deletion happened.
documents.s: How would I delete my account after uninstalling the app?

documents.t: In the billing portal Polar hosts. Polar emails you the link. Billing ends when your account is removed. To stop it sooner, cancel it there.
documents.s: Where do I cancel a plan or change my card?

documents.t: For an ordinary product or legal question, email aoneahsan@gmail.com. Account deletion uses the signed-in page, not email. If the page cannot confirm an outcome, check the account status before you submit again. If that check fails too, write to aoneahsan@gmail.com, and the team can tell you whether a deletion was scheduled; email cannot delete an account.

By the Waylock team · Last updated: 8 November 2026 Yes, as a signed APK for Android 8.0 or newer on the download page. It is not listed on Google Play as of 8 November 2026. Plans are bought on the website through Polar, not in the app. The current Android build identifies itself as version 1.2.0 (code 2), but its route controls still need device checks before these guides can give steps, and Play submission remains open. These guides describe intended controls, not instructions proven on a device.
Revisit this page for a dated update. For an ordinary product question, email the Waylock team. We will update the page after checking the public listing and released app.

By the Waylock team · Last updated: 7 November 2026 Waylock is intended to let you hold a delivery stop in place, choose a range for a trip stop and decide what to do after a wrong turn. Device proof is still missing. Before treating these as available steps, check the release status.
documents.s: How are Waylock routes meant to work?

documents.t: A stop lock is intended to keep one chosen delivery stop in place while the planner reorders other stops around it, subject to the limits you set. Review the estimated order while stopped, before you set off. Times are estimates.
documents.s: How would I keep a delivery stop in position?

documents.t: The Trip planner is intended to find a matching stop within a range measured along the route from the origin or a previous stop. Check the proposed place and route before guidance. A search can find no match.
documents.s: How would I choose a stop within a distance range?

documents.t: Your chosen route is designed to stay visible as an overlay while the Google Navigation SDK may reroute its own guidance, so you can compare a way back with a new route. Stop before choosing. The exact recovery steps for a failed route calculation still need a device test.
documents.s: What would happen after a wrong turn?

documents.t: None yet. The device test must show the actual stop-lock, Trip planner and route-choice controls before the guide can name steps a driver can follow. It must also show what remains safe after a failed route calculation and how the driver recovers. Until then, check the release status.
